clue.text: Metal with yellow colour?

definitions.meaning: a soft bluish-white metallic element, number 48
artists' pigments made from this metal's sulphide give a bright yellow paint

explanation.surface: Someone describes a metal tinted yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The element gives its name to an artists' pigment, so it is both a chemical element and a shade of paint.

clue.text: Teases Charles about folios

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for folio, so FF is folios

explanation.surface: Charles mocks people over some pages of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib or banter with someone is to kid them, a synonym of teasing.

clue.text: Odd role perhaps for idle scribbler

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange part an actor might play as a lazy writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who absent-mindedly draws squiggles is an aimless doodle-maker.

clue.text: Enthusiast elected, having discarded duds

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, an enthusiast or buff who is elected is in, so the buff is 'in'
duds is slang for clothes, so having discarded them means naked

explanation.surface: A fan wins a vote after throwing off some useless items.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: 'the buff' (enthusiast) is 'in' (elected), turned round as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stark naked, the state of someone who has taken off all their clothes.

clue.text: Field sports for airborne types?

parts.note: a meadow is a field
larks are bits of fun or sport

explanation.surface: Outdoor games for those who fly.
explanation.definitionFit: American songbirds that sing in flight are flying creatures, hence airborne types.

clue.text: Hawk drawn by writer on horseback

definitions.meaning: in falconry, a wild hawk caught as an adult and hard to tame
drawn as in gaunt and worn-looking
H. Rider ..., author of King Solomon's Mines: a writer who is a Rider

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is sketched by an author riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the third is a pun, since the novelist's middle name was Rider.
explanation.definitionFit: An untamed adult falcon, a gaunt look, and the novelist Rider Haggard all share this one word.

clue.text: Dance this down in Plymouth

definitions.meaning: add down to this word and you get a lively country dance
Plymouth's seafront promenade is famous, where Drake played bowls

explanation.surface: Someone is told to dance down in a Devon port.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoedown is a country dance; Plymouth Hoe is the clifftop green in the Devon port where Drake reputedly played bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden tool's name begins a dance word and also names Plymouth's famous headland green.

clue.text: Overworking finally wore out Chaucer's poet friend

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word overworking
out as in disordered, so the letters of wore are rearranged

explanation.surface: Excessive toil eventually exhausted a poet who was Chaucer's companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' scrambles the word 'wore' after the last letter of 'Overworking'. John Gower was a 14th-century English poet and friend of Chaucer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gower, poet of Confessio Amantis, was Chaucer's contemporary and friend, to whom Troilus was dedicated.

clue.text: Disposal to quail at this part?

indicators.note: a disposal is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An arrangement to make someone flinch at this stage.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics and chemistry it is a portion that divides the whole exactly, a measured sample.

clue.text: Constable appears to be on the trail of fruit

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
a berry is a fruit

explanation.surface: A police officer seems to be tracking some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogberry is the bumbling constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogberry is the comic chief of the watch in Much Ado About Nothing, a famous fictional policeman.

clue.text: Jack determined to countenance reversal of policy

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able-bodied seaman) is a sailor too
being out to do something means being determined to do it
countenance is the face

explanation.surface: A sailor resolves to put up with a sudden change of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countenance' reads as a verb, to tolerate, but here it is the noun for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn on parade becomes the idiom for a complete change of course in opinion or policy.

clue.text: How to twist the laundry!

parts.note: wet washing is squeezed out by twisting it hard, which is also a word for extorting

explanation.surface: Instructions for twisting the washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezing water from cloth by twisting it is exactly the action described.

clue.text: ASLEF in disorder? That's untrue

indicators.note: letters in disorder are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: ASLEF is a British train drivers' trade union

explanation.surface: Is the train drivers' union in chaos? That is not true.
explanation.walkthrough: ASLEF, the Associated Society of Locomotive Engineers and Firemen, is a British rail union; its 'disorder' sounds like industrial trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong or not true is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Colleague has right to take the strain, as appropriate

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a mate or colleague
a strain is a melody or tune

explanation.surface: A coworker is entitled to bear the pressure, as is only fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests stress, but here it is a musical strain. OPPO, from 'opposite number', is British services slang for a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timely and suitable is well-suited to the occasion, a synonym for fitting.

clue.text: Odd chaps, Albert and Charles, providing food for Israelites

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: Al is a short form of Albert
Charles Lamb was the English essayist who wrote as Elia

explanation.surface: Some peculiar men named Albert and Charles feed the Israelites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges CHAPS plus AL into PASCHAL; Charles Lamb was a Romantic essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamb sacrificed and eaten at Passover is the feast's central dish for the Jewish people.

clue.text: Mediator has problems with time-signal

parts.note: troubles are problems
a hooter, like a factory siren, signals the start or end of a shift

explanation.surface: A peacemaker is beset by difficulties with a clock signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sorts out disputes or faults is a fixer who settles difficulties between parties.

clue.text: Applause all round Ewell, I hear, for egg-producers' achievement

indicators.note: all round says the applause wraps right round the next piece

parts.note: an ovation is applause

indicators.note: I hear tells us to go by the sound of the place name

parts.note: Ewell, a town in Surrey, said aloud is the two letters U and L

explanation.surface: Clapping breaks out around a Surrey town, I gather, for a feat of hens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' turns Ewell, a Surrey town, into the letters U L, which go inside OVATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing an egg from the ovary is what egg-producing females accomplish, the biological event of egg release.

clue.text: Gushing letter, it's said, I've written about us

indicators.note: written about means the words before are set down around the next piece

parts.note: the letter F is spelt out as it is spoken
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An overflowing letter, they say, which I wrote about the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' spells the letter F as spoken; 'written about' wraps that and 'I've' round 'us'. The surface's letter is correspondence, not the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusive praise pours out unrestrained, so it is overflowing and gushing.

clue.text: Courses enjoyed by brainy types?

parts.note: courses read as dishes of a meal, served to intellectuals, i.e. matter to ponder

explanation.surface: Academic courses taken by clever students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests study, but read as a meal's courses it gives the idiom for something worth thinking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives one ideas to ponder is pictured as a meal for the mind.

clue.text: Japanese island gives no stock away in Scotland

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for no
stock in the sense of family line, kin
awa is Scots for away

explanation.surface: A Japanese island hands out no livestock across the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is the largest of Japan's Ryukyu Islands, an island of Japan.

clue.text: There was no holding Harry!

parts.note: the famous escapologist Harry could slip any chains, locks or cells

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an unstoppable man named Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Houdini was the great escape artist: no restraint could hold him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian-born American escapologist was famous for breaking free of every restraint.

clue.text: Show great respect to Paul as rider

definitions.meaning: Paul ... made the midnight ride of 1775 warning that the British were coming

explanation.surface: Honour Paul for his horsemanship.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to honour deeply, and Paul Revere is the American patriot famed for his ride.

clue.text: Cook ruins veal joint so-called

indicators.note: cook in the sense of falsify or rework, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef spoils a veal joint, as it is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the chef but is the anagram signal; 'joint' looks like meat but is a mechanical coupling.
explanation.definitionFit: A universal joint is a flexible coupling between shafts, so the adjective names that kind of joint.

clue.text: Do better than 40 in Rome, say

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the letters sound

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Outshine forty in Rome, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, the Roman numeral letters X L give the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo or surpass others is to outshine them, i.e. perform better.

clue.text: Going round America, Lincoln discovers malpractice

indicators.note: going round tells us one piece encircles the other

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: Touring the States, President Lincoln uncovers wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or corrupt use of a position is misuse, which is what wrongdoing in office amounts to.

clue.text: Is a pay-claim the only issue for Sarah?

parts.note: taken as written
an account (AC) is a bill, a claim for payment

explanation.surface: A wage demand seems to be the single matter on Sarah's mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a topic but means offspring: in Genesis Sarah bore Abraham one son.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Sarah's sole child with Abraham was this son, so he is her only offspring.

clue.text: British scientist tending to wait on this, say

indicators.note: say signals that we go by how the words sound

parts.note: with wait heard as weight, the side bearing the weight is the heavy side

explanation.surface: A British scientist inclined to linger here.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Heaviside was an English physicist (the Heaviside layer). 'Wait' must be heard as 'weight' to reach the heavy side.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Heaviside was an English electrical engineer and physicist, an example of a British scientist.

clue.text: Hospital at Homburg?

explanation.surface: A hospital in the German spa town of Homburg.
explanation.walkthrough: Homburg looks like the town in Germany, but it is a felt hat with a dented crown, named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A homburg is a kind of felt headwear, an example of the general item, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Something shouldered by oriental missionary and foreign follower

parts.note: E is short for east, so oriental
Saint Paul was the great missionary of the early Church
et is French and Latin for and, the word that leads on to what follows

explanation.surface: An Eastern missionary and his overseas disciple carry something on their shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform is literally worn on the shoulder.

clue.text: Where Guy's memory still shines bright

definitions.text: Where Guy's memory still shines bright

parts.words: Where Guy's memory still shines bright
parts.note: Guy Fawkes is remembered each 5 November in Britain with outdoor fires on which his effigy burns

explanation.surface: A tribute to a man whose memory remains vivid.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes plotted to blow up Parliament in 1605; Britons burn a 'guy' on outdoor fires every 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: The great outdoor blaze of Guy Fawkes Night is literally where his memory burns brightly.
